Existence and necessity of a finite-second-moment stationary law follow from contraction and nonzero centered innovations. A strictly decreasing root function establishes unique V*>0. Cauchy–Schwarz proves the global minimum and equality conditions establish unique full-support probabilities. Exact-rational verification independently confirms the triple V*=1/15 versus 1/3, 288 other covariance cases and 9053 finite-grid comparisons; the finite checks are not substituted for the general proof.

value.rationale: The global design problem is naturally motivated by the gap between variance-minimizing gradient sampling and actual long-run constant-step optimization error. The theorem provides a unique computable optimum for every noninterpolating m-component scalar quadratic and entire admissible stepsize interval; a zero-residual yet high-curvature component gets majority optimal sampling mass, and the optimal design cuts stationary error by exactly a factor of five in a natural simple example. These are structural and quantitative, not a routine endpoint check.
